title: DNA double helix
subtitle: Two complementary strands, carrying an ordered sequence
description: DNA is built from repeating units called nucleotides. Each has a sugar, a base and, along the chain, a phosphate connection. The bases are named A, T, G and C. Here two synthetic strands each contain the sequence CGCGAATTCGCG, read in their own 5′ to 3′ direction.
explanation: DNA is built from repeating units called nucleotides. Each has a sugar, a base and, along the chain, a phosphate connection. The bases are named A, T, G and C. Here two synthetic strands each contain the sequence CGCGAATTCGCG, read in their own 5′ to 3′ direction.

The two strands run in opposite directions. A pairs with T; G pairs with C. Strong chemical links, called covalent bonds, connect each strand. Weaker attractions, called hydrogen bonds, join matching bases across the gap. Stacking the flat bases also helps stabilize the helix. The deposited atom positions show a real, slightly irregular shape rather than a perfect mathematical spiral.

This is a short DNA crystal reference, not a person’s genome, a tumour sample or a whole chromosome. It helps explain molecular structure. It cannot show which genes a cancer cell uses or establish whether a treatment works.
limits: Synthetic 12-base-pair DNA crystal fragment; water is omitted. This is neither a human genome sample nor a whole chromosome. Static coordinates cannot establish gene activity, tumour behaviour or treatment benefit.

metadata.organism: Synthetic DNA; no source organism assigned
metadata.mutationNote: Entry is engineered/synthetic; RCSB polymer-entity metadata reports zero mutations. This does not mean it is an unmodified biological sample.
metadata.omissions: All HETATM records (water) and crystallographic symmetry copies. Hydrogens and absent terminal phosphates are not added.

alternateLocations.policy: Highest occupancy for each atom; ties prefer blank then A; preserve file order thereafter.

metadata.coordinates: Deposited Cartesian coordinates retained without reflection, smoothing, relaxation or rescaling. Units are angstroms (1 Å = 0.1 nm).
metadata.stereochemistry: Inherited from deposited coordinates and residue identity; no stereocentres, missing atoms, hydrogens or protonation states are generated.
metadata.bonds: Within-residue connectivity and order from deposited _chem_comp_bond; sequential polymer C–N or O3′–P links added by known chain order and checked for plausible length. Disulfides and hydrogen contacts come from deposited _struct_conn. No distance-only bond inference.
metadata.bondDrawing: A single stick indicates connectivity; displayed stick count need not encode deposited bond order. Atom spheres are illustrative, not measured surfaces.
metadata.backbone: Guide links between successive C4' atoms in each chain. These are not direct chemical bonds or measured surfaces.
metadata.contacts: Deposited donor/acceptor heavy-atom pairs for Watson–Crick hydrogen bonds; not hydrogen-atom coordinates and not covalent interstrand bonds.
